subject: Unexpected 429 surge during weekday peak — remediation & credit request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@apexanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected 429s during Tue–Wed peak — immediate remediation steps and next steps

Hi Samir —

First, I want to apologize for the disruption you saw during your weekday peak window on Tue/Wed. We take availability and predictable throughput seriously, and I know any 429s during your ETL run are unacceptable.

What we know so far: our preliminary investigation shows an accidental mapping of one of Apex's tenant IDs to a legacy burst quota bucket. That mapping caused your traffic pattern to be evaluated against a much smaller burst window than intended, producing a higher-than-expected rate of 429 rejections during concurrent spikes. We've captured the relevant logs and a config diff (attached) for your review.

Short-term actions already taken (complete):
- Temporary quota bump applied to your tenant to prevent further rejections during peak windows.
- Routing rule corrected to point to your standard quota namespace (fix deployed 08:14 PST).
- Support ticket SUP-7890 opened and linked to this thread; we attached representative log snippets for your ops team.

Planned next steps (this week):
- We will run a one-hour replay of the affected window under controlled conditions to validate the fix (scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 PST).
- A proposed customer credit to compensate for failed requests is attached as a short summary PDF. We want to get something fair on the books quickly — happy to adjust if your team prefers a different structure (usage credit vs. one-time invoice credit).

Would you be available for a 30-minute postmortem call on Friday 11:00 PST to walk through findings and agree next steps? If that time doesn't work, propose alternatives and we'll accommodate.

Attachments: 429-investigation-log-snippet.txt, config-diff-20270603.json, proposed-credit-summary.pdf

Again, I'm sorry for the impact. We'll make sure the remediation is documented and we implement a preventive guard so this doesn't recur.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Samir Patel <samir@apexanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s during Tue–Wed peak — immediate remediation steps and next steps

Thanks Vanessa.

We saw a ~23% failure rate for the 02:00–04:00 UTC batch window (our ETL hangs and retries aggressively, which ripples into downstream SLAs). The temporary bump stopped new errors, but we need:
1) concrete evidence we can share with internal procurement for a credit (logs + a short write-up);
2) confirmation the mapping change is permanent and won't be reverted by automated config pushes on your side.

If you can send the replay results and a write-up before Friday, that will help move approval faster. 11:00 PST Friday works for the call.

— Samir
Head of Platform, Apex Analytics
ops@apexanalytics.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected 429s — internal RCA + proposed customer credit

Team — forwarding Samir's note. Quick internal summary and asks:

Root cause summary (short): config aliasing bug caused tenant routing to pick up legacy burst namespace. That legacy namespace had a 60s short burst window configured accidentally during a prior migration; the correct namespace uses a 5m sliding window. When Apex's parallelization peaked, the shorter window hit the burst limit and produced 429s.

Evidence attached: config-diff-20270603.json shows the alias link; 429-investigation-log-snippet.txt includes repeated 429 responses keyed by tenant id.

Immediate asks: 
- Karthik: confirm the permanent config push and add an automated diff check to prevent alias regressions (can you triage a quick change to the validation pipeline by EOD?).
- Priyom: can you own the replay validation tomorrow at 10:00 PST and generate a short 'replay report' with before/after success rates? Put the report in the Drive link and mark as "replay-report-apex-20270604".
- Lauren: work with finance on a proposed credit number. The attached proposed-credit-summary.pdf is a starting point (we're suggesting a usage credit equal to the failed tokens + 10% goodwill). If procurement pushes back, prepare a one-line explanation we can send them summarizing the technical cause (I drafted below).

Draft blurb for procurement (short):
"A misrouted quota alias caused a shorter enforcement window to be applied to Apex traffic during two high-concurrency windows. Redwood implemented an immediate fix (routing restored, temporary quota bump) and will issue a compensatory usage credit for affected transactions. Additional automated validation will be added to prevent similar config alias regressions."

I'll own communications back to Samir once we have the replay report and a credit figure. Keep this tight — Samir needs the documentation for internal approvals.

— Vanessa

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@apexanalytics.com>, Apex Analytics Ops <ops@apexanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Unexpected 429s during Tue–Wed peak — remediation complete and credit proposal

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for your patience. Follow-up with completed items and links below:

Completed validation and findings:
- Replay run (2027-06-04 10:00 PST) executed by Priyom: before fix fail rate 22.7%; after fix 0.3%. Replay report uploaded: https://drive.google.com/redwood/apex-429-evidence (file name: replay-report-apex-20270604.pdf).
- Root cause confirmed: alias->legacy-burst mapping (see config-diff-20270603.json). The legacy burst window was an accidental carry-over; the mapping has been removed and the correct 5m window enforced.
- Preventive measures: added a diff-check to the config CI that rejects alias changes without an explicit migration flag; added an alert if per-tenant burst-window < 3m. Karthik owned the push and validated in staging.

Credit proposal and next steps:
- Attached: proposed-credit-summary.pdf (summary: usage credit equal to failed requests during the incident period + 10% goodwill).
- We can apply the credit as a one-time invoice credit or as account balance — whichever you prefer.

Requested confirmation:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the proposed credit (reply to this thread) and select "invoice credit" or "account balance".
2) Confirm whether you want the replay report and config diffs redacted for sharing with your procurement team; we can provide an abbreviated technical memo if needed for vendor review.

I'll run the Friday postmortem at 11:00 PST as scheduled; invitation to follow. If procurement needs a short sign-off memo before then, I can convert the draft blurb into a one-page note.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the partnership and will follow through on the corrective actions.

Attachments: proposed-credit-summary.pdf, replay-report-apex-20270604.pdf, config-diff-20270603.json

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
